task.description:

Implement the PASSed design at lib/letflow/design/iss0881-sandbox-pool-test-isolation.md exactly -- it is CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved, so implement what it specifies rather than re-deciding the approach. Read the design doc in full before writing any code.

This is a test-file-only change to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs: replace every platform-wide `sandbox_schema_names() == baseline`-style equality assertion with the scoped membership/diff checks the design specifies at each call site it enumerates (RT-6, RT-3, the ISS-0292/RT-8 diff-order test, and any others the design names), widening pattern matches to capture each test's own schema name(s) where the design says to. Do NOT touch lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex -- the design confirms no production code change is needed, and doing so would be out of this fix's scope.

After implementing: run `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (must be clean) and `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` (must be green -- this is the existing, non-flaky-under-isolation baseline; the actual regression-proof-under-contention comes later at Step 4, not from you). Report the real output of both.

Complete the handoff yourself (claim IN_PROGRESS first) with a real result block, do not touch the task block, commit your implementation + the completed handoff to the feature branch and push, run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir handoffs/WF03-ISS0881-20260929` before finishing. next_action should point to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 3b) -- note in your summary that this is a test-only change touching no tenant-data path, API route, migration, or secret, so SECURITY-REVIEWER's own scope test is expected to find it NOT APPLICABLE, but SECURITY-REVIEWER still runs and states that itself; you do not get to skip it. Leave the checkout on feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929.

result.summary: Implemented the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-approved design at lib/letflow/design/iss0881-sandbox-pool-test-isolation.md exactly, touching only test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex untouched, confirmed by git diff --stat). Every call site the design enumerates was updated: RT-1 (deleted the bare `assert final == baseline` at the old line 846, kept the `refute MapSet.member?` leak check); RT-2 (widened the :o and w1 pattern matches to bind `o_schema`/`w1_schema`, replaced the platform-wide equality with two `refute MapSet.member?` checks); RT-3 (split into a positive-presence membership check plus `assert map_size(state.active) == 1` for the mid-test assertion, and a `refute MapSet.member?` for the post-release leak check); RT-4, RT-5, RT-6 (deleted the redundant `assert final == baseline` line in each, keeping the existing `refute MapSet.member?` check unchanged); RT-7 (widened the :o and :w claims to bind `o_schema`/`w_schema`, replaced the equality with two membership refutes); RT-8 (widened the :o1 and :a claims to bind `o1_schema`/`a_schema`, replaced the equality with two membership refutes); RT-9 (no change, per the design -- no equality assertion exists there); and the ISS-0292/RT-8 critical-regression test (added `Enum.filter(&(&1 in [first_schema, middle_schema, third_schema]))` to the diff pipeline before the exact-order equality assertion). Verified no `== baseline` or `MapSet.put(baseline` call sites remain (grep, zero matches). No deviation from the design was needed. Ran `mix format` on the file afterward (one line-wrapping reflow on the RT-8 assert_receive, functionally identical) and reconfirmed compile+test green post-format. Real command output: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0 with no warnings. `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` -> `Result: 23 passed`, exit code 0 (re-run twice, including once post-format, both green; log shows the expected ISS-0292 retry_query_once/resilient_drop_schema warnings from that describe block's own deliberately-triggered failures, not test failures). This is a test-file-only change touching no tenant-data path, API route, migration, or secret, so SECURITY-REVIEWER's own scope test is expected to find it NOT APPLICABLE -- it still must run and state that itself.
